disposition_reason: Controlled cultivation study of 59 oyster mushroom production strains on wheat-straw substrate reporting cap and stipe metal contents (Tables 3-5) and a sodium selenate fortification trial on one strain (Table 6).

study.design: Experimental cultivation under identical model conditions; selenium fortification trial
study.origin: Grown in a controlled growing unit, Slovak University of Agriculture in Nitra, Slovakia; strains from culture collections and market isolates
study.method: Microwave HNO3/H2O2 digestion, ICP-OES (iCAP 7600); Hg by AMA 254; Se by ET-AAS
study.qa: NIST SRM 1570a spinach leaves, recovery 95.2% (Se and Hg methods)

unresolved: Table 6 lead and cadmium columns are marked * with the note 'Source: * Author of the work [23]', i.e. from the authors' 2019 paper; they are treated as quoted values and not extracted (Pb 0.97-1.90, Cd 0.18-0.25 mg/kg DM).
Cadmium, lead, nickel, chromium and mercury were not reported for the 59-strain survey despite being in the method validation table.
Macro elements Ca, K, Mg, Na in Tables 3-5 were not extracted.
Text gives the lowest cap/stipe Cu as 1.7 (strain 29) and highest cap Cu as 12.0, while Tables 4-5 print 1.8 and 18.0; tables used.
Wet-ash substrate values in the discussion are quoted from another study and not extracted.
